---
title: "squirrels.qmd"
---
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(cowsay)
set.seed(42)

#Display how many times a squirrel successfully raided a bird feeder
attempts <- sample(c("Success","Failure"), size = 150, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.3,0.7))
n_successes <- sum(attempts == "Success")
say(paste("I, Steve the Squirrel, successfully raided the bird feeder ", n_successes, " times!"), by = "squirrel")

#Simulate for 1000 squirrels, table and plot
combined_successes <- c()
for (i in seq_len(1000)) {
  is_success <- sample(c("SUCCESS", "FAILURE"),
    size = 150,
    replace = TRUE,
    prob = c(0.3, 0.7)
  )
  n_successes <- sum(is_success == "SUCCESS")
  combined_successes <- c(combined_successes, n_successes)
}
print(combined_successes)
df_squirrels <- tibble("N_Successful_Heists" = combined_successes)
gt(head(df_squirrels))

ggplot(df_squirrels, aes(x = N_Successful_Heists)) + geom_bar() + ggtitle("Number of Successful Heists per Squirrel - Simulated") + xlab("Number of successful heists") + ylab("Number of squirrels") + theme_minimal()

#Calculate probabiltiy of success for each value of k using binomial distribution
probs <- c()
for(k in seq(0, 150))
{
  prob_X_equals_k <- dbinom(k, 150, 0.3)
  probs <- c(probs, prob_X_equals_k)
}

#Put probabilities into a dataframe and plot distribution function
probability_dataframe <- tibble(N_Successful_Heists = seq(0, 150), Probability = probs)
ggplot(probability_dataframe, aes(x = N_Successful_Heists, y = Probability)) + geom_col() + ggtitle("Binomial Distribution of Successful Heists - Theoretical") + xlab("Number of successful heists") + ylab("Probabiltiy") + theme_minimal()

#Simulate 1000 datasets of 200 flowers with a 60% chance of being pollinated
flowers <- rbinom(n = 1000, size = 200, prob = 0.6)
enough_for_experiment <- sum(flowers >= 125)
probability_success <- enough_for_experiment/1000
print(probability_success)

#Check answer using pbinom()
probability_enough <- 1 - pbinom(124, 200, 0.6)
print(probability_enough)

#Find number of flowers needed for 95% probability of having enough pollinated flowers
probs2 <- c()
for(i in seq(200,250))
{
  prob_125_or_over <- 1 - pbinom(124, i, 0.6)
  probs2 <- c(probs2, prob_125_or_over)
}
probs_df <- tibble(npicked = seq(200,250), psuccess = probs2)
#Filter for rows where probability of success is >95%
probs_df_filt <- probs_df |> filter(psuccess >= 0.95)
gt(probs_df_filt)
#Conclusion: she needs to pick 228 flowers
```
